correctness.rationale: For any n>=2,c in (0,1), the unique root is in (c²,1). Its radical defines positive a<b. The complete John containment reduces to a concave quadratic q(s), whose unique maximizer s=1/sqrt(n) has value 1. The normalized contact vectors (±1/sqrt(n),±sqrt((n-1)/n)e_j), each assigned weight n/[4(n-1)], give zero mean and identity second moment; John theorem proves global optimality, including non-symmetric competitors. The containing ellipsoid inequality reduces to 1-[2c/(1+c)]s(1-s)<=1, and ±e_i supply the Löwner identity contact condition. Quadratic expansions prove both limits. Sample verifier executed; finite tests not offered as proofs.

value.rationale: Equal-ball lenses are canonical sharp minimizers of the newly resolved reverse-isoperimetric problem. The two volume-extremal ellipsoids are standard natural affine-geometric approximations to that class, with previously unlisted exact axes and full contact sets. The high-dimensional axial contraction, √n a → (1-c²)/c despite b→√(1-c²), and the sharp shrinking-lens ratios are meaningful geometric limit phenomena.
